title: Claude Code MCP OAuth redirects can disclose refresh tokens to another host
summary: The Claude Code 2.1.321 changelog fixes MCP OAuth requests sending secrets, including refresh tokens, to another host when redirected by a server.

severity.rationale: The documented flaw exposes authentication secrets across hosts during MCP OAuth. Credential exposure warrants a 72-hour response.

affected.note: The changelog names the fixing release but does not establish the first affected version.

exposure: MCP OAuth flows receiving server redirects are the documented exposure condition; the vendor does not identify a narrower affected platform.

params.instructions: Run claude --version and confirm 2.1.321 or later; check MCP OAuth usage when assessing exposure to redirects.

remediation.details: Update Claude Code to 2.1.321 or later. As a containment recommendation, revoke and replace OAuth grants if their secrets may have been disclosed.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updating or containment can interrupt dependent workflows.

verification: Confirm the installed and running component meets the documented fix or containment condition.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
Removed source support claims for identifiers and vendor severity that the changelog does not supply.
